title: STILL PRESENT (r3): the wrong-person TOCTOU is open — apply_wrong_person still executes the unguarded update_reference_call_status; mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql has ZERO production callers and the race pin calls the guarded SQL directly (vacuous)
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:1248-1257: `False ->
              case
                sql.update_reference_call_status(
                  config.db,
                  id_uuid,
                  sql.AwaitingCorrection,
                  "",
                  "contact_invalid",
                  sql.ContactInitiated,
                )` — update_reference_call_status.sql:22-24: `WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status` (no taken_over_at clause) — take_over_reference_call.sql: `-- Deliberately writes ONLY taken_over_at + next_attempt_at, never status:` (so a taken-over row still matches the status-only WHERE) — grep: mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person( is called ONLY from the test (lines 1746, 1758), never by a handler — test line 1745-1746: `let assert Ok(returned) =
    rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)`
detail: Executed awaiting arm still races: take-over between the token read and the UPDATE matches (status unchanged by take-over) and yanks the landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction. Dedicated guarded SQL is dead code; the pin tests the SQL, not the POST path, so it cannot catch the unwired backstop.
recommended_fix: Replace update_reference_call_status in apply_wrong_person's awaiting arm with sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person; re-point the race test to drive the /reference/:token/wrong-person POST (or apply_wrong_person) so neutralizing the executed UPDATE turns it red.
